text:
marco (product): Quick catchup on private deploy rollout when customers bring their own networking + DNS/certs. Need a defined upgrade choreography and fallback behavior for customers who can't preserve stable egress or who have ephemeral NAT pools. Goal: ship a minimal, auditable path that reduces support blurbs.
sarah (solutions): Field note: customers often refuse topology changes. They ask for an upgrade that doesn't require a re-IP or re-cert. We should avoid rejoining clusters.
toni (netops): Constraints: some customers have rotating NAT pools (~6-24h), others have strict egress ACLs tied to IP lists. Proposal: staged upgrade with three modes: 1) preserve-egress (preferred), 2) soft-relay (temporary relay for control-plane only), 3) full-relay (all outbound through relay).
devon (eng): Implementation sketch: installer writes a small control plane adapter that can operate in two modes. It can add a sidecar that tunnels control-plane calls to Redwood relay for full-relay, or it flips iptables SNAT preservation rules for preserve-egress. Runtime toggle via control plane API.
marco (product): Good. For upgrade safety we want: canary -> broad rollout -> fast rollback. Canary should be per-tenant and validate: egress identity, cert continuity, and request latency.
sarah (solutions): Add acceptance checks: TLS cert fingerprint matches pre-upgrade for control endpoint, observed egress IPs within expected pool, and no 5xx error spike >0.5% in 10m window.
toni (netops): We'll need packet capture snippets and a short diagnostic script for customers to run post-upgrade. Also require a "egress-probe" that spits out: observed_ips, dns_resolution, tls_fingerprint.
devon (eng): Example installer snippet we can publish in docs:

```
# values.yaml (installer)
networking:
  mode: preserve-egress # preserve-egress | soft-relay | full-relay
  egress:
    expected_cidr: 203.0.113.0/28 # optional, used for validation
  dns_handshake:
    control_fqdn: control.redwood.example
    cert_thumbprint: "SHA256:abcd..."
```

marco (product): For launch criteria draft:
- docs: handshake checklist + values.yaml examples + troubleshooting FAQ (PR ready)
- installer: runtime toggle + canary rollout support + diagnostic probe
- tests: automated canary that simulates NAT rotation and verifies rollback triggers
- validation: 3 field pilots (1 preserve-egress, 1 soft-relay, 1 full-relay) with signed acceptance
- observability: spike/delta alerts and an egress-identity dashboard

sarah (solutions): Also include a short customer-facing flowchart: "Do you control egress IPs? -> Yes: preserve-egress path. No: soft-relay option." It saves repeated explanations.
toni (netops): Edge case: double-NAT + ISP rewriting source port. Detection: mismatch between proc-net stats and observed external IP. I'll add detection heuristics to runbook.
devon (eng): Edge case: customers behind an outbound proxy that rewrites SNI. For that, force TLS passthrough and include a certificate pinning option. We'll document the caveats.
marco (product): Action items:
- marco: draft public handshake doc + flowchart (today)
- toni: runbook skeleton + diagnostic scripts (Thu COB)
- devon: PR for runtime toggle + canary automation (start tomorrow, 2 sprints)
- sarah: coordinate pilots and collect acceptance criteria (by Mon)

ops-bot: deployment -> env=staging, job=egress-probe v2.0 scheduled :white_check_mark:

marco (product): Let's keep the default conservative: ship with soft-relay enabled as fallback, preserve-egress opt-in. That reduces failed installs for customers who didn't read the preflight doc. We'll finalize at Fri sync. Drop any remaining risks.
toni (netops): Risk: customers expecting static IP lists for firewall allowlists may still break. We'll require a signed form for those customers that we test preserve-egress with their netops team.
devon (eng): Risk: latency/egress costs for full-relay. We'll instrument cost-estimates in console per-tenant.
sarah (solutions): Customer ask: ability to flip to full-relay for maintenance windows without a reinstall. We support a control-plane toggle that reconciles in ~1-2 minutes. Note that customers must approve the security implications.
marco (product): Noted. I'll include that as a recommended practice in the docs. Thanks all, will capture minutes and send a short decision doc.
